source_assessment: Net2Net (Chen,Goodfellow,Shlens; ICLR 2016 arXiv 1511.05641) proposes function-preserving wider/deeper initialization via weight replication with divisor correction (Net2WiderNet) and identity-insertion deepening under ReLU (Net2DeeperNet). It reports this accelerates iterative design/lifelong scaling plus a failed FitNets-style hidden-layer prediction auxiliary loss. Transferable sub-ideas here: (1) safe immediate no-regression capacity expansion; (2) symmetry-breaking noise after replication; (3) architecture-dependent remapping constraints e.g. BN-style per-channel coupling; (4) the negative result itself. Source is image classification supervised; it says nothing about this scored correlation metric, clipping, warm-up, group-disjoint folds, or sequence reset. Treat as inspiration only.

ideas.title: Warm-up-wide: function-preserving widening of the recurrent blend hidden state
ideas.source_component_and_location: Net2Net Section 2.3 (Net2WiderNet) and Section 2.2 divisor correction for replication
ideas.proposed_change: Treat current deterministic recurrent-model blend as teacher and create wider student by replicating subset of recurrent/hidden units replication divisor so pre-insertion mapping is preserved, then add small noise to extra copies and continue training there rather scratch.
ideas.assumptions: A teacher blend can be expressed as parameterizable net worth widening; replication divisor correction is implementable deployed recurrent parameterization; continued training improves beyond teacher in-fold data.
ideas.cheapest_discriminating_test: On single local historical fold, compare (a) normal retraining of equally wide model its own init versus (b) function-preserving widened student fine-tuned, equal compute budget; measure local1 validation pooled correlation and early-epoch convergence speed.
ideas.matched_control: Same target capacity trained random init identical optimizer/hyperparameters and compute budget.
ideas.falsifier: If (b) does not beat (a) within budget, or its initial post-insertion score is not least as good as teacher, function-preserving premise is not helping here.
ideas.resource_estimate: Cheap: one fold, modest widen factor, CPU/low VRAM, no sequence identity leakage.
ideas.suggested_parent_direction: Child of deterministic recurrent blend recipe; deepen widening only stable teacher exists.

ideas.title: Deeper-recurrent insertion: ReLU-identity layer insertion inside recurrence
ideas.source_component_and_location: Net2Net Section 2.4 (Net2DeeperNet), identity under ReLU and BN identity-setting caveat
ideas.proposed_change: Where recurrence/transformations use ReLU-like behavior, insert extra layer initialized to approximate identity (e.g. identity init) to deepen model without immediate function change, then allow it to learn; if normalization is present, set scale/bias to neutralize normalization statistics.
ideas.assumptions: Local nonlinearities admit identity-insertion preserves function insertion; deeper parameterization can later capture structure shallow blend misses.
ideas.cheapest_discriminating_test: Insert one identity-initialized layer chosen point, verify pre-training outputs match teacher held-out slice within tolerance, then compare fine-tuned deeper model to depth-matched baseline trained scratch.
ideas.matched_control: Depth-matched model same extra layer but random init.
ideas.falsifier: If deeper net does not surpass depth-matched random-init control, or insertion breaks output equality beyond tolerance, deepening transfer is moot.
ideas.resource_estimate: Cheap per fold: limited depth increase, local compute only.
ideas.suggested_parent_direction: Deeper variant of recurrent blend; gated by identity-insertion feasibility check.

ideas.title: Channel-coupled widening with symmetry-breaking schedule for recurrent feature maps
ideas.source_component_and_location: Net2Net Section 2.3 constraints for batch-norm-style coupling and the noise-addition recommendation after replication
ideas.proposed_change: When widening per-channel/computed feature maps, tie remapping of weights to associated scale/shift parameters so new channel does not mix one unit's weights another's normalization, and add controlled noise schedule to extra copies so they diverge duplicated behavior.
ideas.assumptions: The deployed model has coupled parameters analogous to BN-style scaling must be remapped consistently; symmetry breaking helps unused capacity learn.
ideas.cheapest_discriminating_test: Ablate coupling vs no-coupling and noise vs no-noise during widen-and-fine-tune one fold; check whether unconstrained widening degrades early stability or final local metric.
ideas.matched_control: Widening without coupling constraints and/or without added noise.
ideas.falsifier: If coupling has no effect and noise either destabilizes or does not improve, mechanism transfers little.
ideas.resource_estimate: Cheap: mostly engineering on one fold.
ideas.suggested_parent_direction: Refinement of widening idea, gated existence of coupled parameters.

ideas.title: Unconventional: warm-start prediction-head distillation from a no-gradient teacher blend, risking the source's negative result
ideas.mechanism_family: auxiliary teacher-prediction loss (distillation-style) - explicitly the source's failed path
ideas.source_component_and_location: Net2Net Section 2.1 (Feature Prediction), the FitNets-like hidden/prediction-layer auxiliary loss negative result
ideas.proposed_change: Deliberately test method paper reports as unhelpful: add auxiliary terms encouraging student hidden representations/predictions to track deterministic teacher blend, then train real forecasting objective; include safety net to disable aux terms if they hurt.
ideas.assumptions: The negative result ICLR ImageNet+Batchnorm context may not hold this recurrent blend, metric, and warmup regime; auxiliary alignment could stabilize fine-tuning of larger student.
ideas.cheapest_discriminating_test: Small sweep of auxiliary weight one fold comparing student-with-aux vs plain fine-tuned student vs teacher; stop early if aux underperforms no-aux.
ideas.matched_control: Same student without auxiliary teacher-prediction loss.
ideas.falsifier: If aux loss never improves no-aux control and/or degrades early behavior, this inherits source's negative result and should be dropped.
ideas.resource_estimate: Cheap: low extra memory/compute for one fold; risk of worthless result acknowledged.
ideas.suggested_parent_direction: High-risk low-cost probe, only as child of teacher blend if capacity growth is already planned.
